tagline: Make a language model service meet its latency objectives at the lowest cost you can defend, with quality held in Arabic and English
description: Participants take the bilingual visitor assistant of a fictional national events authority, too slow at evening peaks and too costly, and make it meet its service objective at the lowest cost they can defend. They build a first-principles cost model, measure goodput curves on replayed traffic, diagnose seeded bottlenecks, then apply batching, caching, quantisation, speculative decoding, distillation, routing, disaggregated serving and autoscaling, re-running an Arabic and English task evaluation after every change.
audience: Specialists. Engineers who have completed the level 300 core or can show equivalent work: a production AI system they built, operated and can defend.
prerequisites: AE-305 Operating Machine Learning and Language Model Systems
AE-307 Container Orchestration and Cloud Infrastructure for AI Workloads
Has served an open-weight model behind an HTTP endpoint and load-tested it
Computes percentiles and reads a latency histogram
Estimates memory from parameter count and numeric precision

outcomes.text: Compute prefill cost, decode cost and key-value cache memory, and predict the binding resource, given a model card, an accelerator specification sheet and a traffic profile
outcomes.evidence: a sizing sheet whose predicted concurrency limit is within 25% of a measured run

outcomes.text: Evaluate a serving configuration by measuring its goodput curve over concurrency against latency objectives, given an engine, a small open-weight model and a replayed synthetic trace
outcomes.evidence: a repeatable curve of at least seven points with raw data and run-to-run variance

outcomes.text: Diagnose why a deployment misses its service objective and confirm the fix, given three seeded faults: queueing, preemption under cache pressure and prefill interference
outcomes.evidence: a diagnosis per fault with its evidence, and a rerun that meets the objective

outcomes.text: Optimise batching, admission, prefix caching and cache precision while holding task quality, given a multi-tenant trace and Arabic and English evaluation sets
outcomes.evidence: before-and-after goodput, cost per million tokens and quality with intervals, and a passed cross-tenant cache test

outcomes.text: Evaluate quantised, distilled and speculative-decoding variants against the base model and decide which to serve, given a quality floor per language and a cost target
outcomes.evidence: a quality and cost table by language and a one-page serving decision

outcomes.text: Design and defend a serving topology covering disaggregation, routing, replica count and scaling policy, given a daily demand pattern, a service objective and a budget
outcomes.evidence: a design document with predicted and measured goodput and cost per successful request

case_study.name: Liwan National Events Authority
case_study.summary: Musamir, the bilingual visitor assistant of a fictional national events authority, serves three event organisers from one leased accelerator and is too slow at evening peaks and too costly. Every lab works on the same synthetic data: 40,000 Arabic and English visitor requests over a day, model cards and spec sheets, recorded evaluation outcomes for six model variants and a course simulator of the serving engine, all generated with a fixed seed.

format_note: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task

capstone.summary: Tune a provided under-performing deployment of the case assistant to meet its latency objectives at minimum cost per successful request, submitted as a public repository with raw benchmark data, quality by language and a design document, and defended in 20 minutes. The follow-up task repeats the method on the participant's own deployment or a public trace
